items.title: US consumer confidence rises for first time in four months
items.feedTitle: US Consumer Confidence Rises for First Time in Four Months
items.summary: The Conference Board's Consumer Confidence Index rose from 84.2 in September to 91.7 in October, marking the first monthly increase in four months as Americans' views of present and future business conditions improved. The uptick reflects some easing of economic headwinds, though concerns remain about inflation and employment.

cards.title: When consensus masks uncertainty
cards.insight: High confidence in a decision often masks underlying disagreement among experts. Netanyahu's military chiefs opposed a pre-election Iran strike while political leadership pushed for it—a classic split between institutional expertise and political urgency.
cards.takeaway: Before committing to a major decision, explicitly separate the views of those with technical expertise from those with political or financial stakes. Dissenters are valuable, not obstacles.

cards.title: The illusion of early signals
cards.insight: Consumer confidence rose sharply in one month after falling for three, but this doesn't establish a trend. Similarly, early voting or single polls can mislead about broader electoral momentum. One data point is anecdote, not pattern.
cards.takeaway: Require at least two independent validations of a signal before shifting strategy. Demand evidence of consistency, not just direction.

cards.title: Redistricting's lesson on unintended consequences
cards.insight: Republicans designed congressional districts to lock in advantage, but are now spending heavily to defend seats they expected to win easily. The system backfired because districts that are too safe create backlash or energize opposition.
cards.takeaway: When designing systems (markets, organizations, districts), account for how the other side will adapt. Overoptimization for one scenario creates vulnerability to others.

cards.title: Governance structures shape long-term outcomes
cards.insight: Anthropic's IPO filing reveals an unusual governance design intended to preserve founder control and AI safety priorities even after public listing. This acknowledges that normal board and shareholder structures might override founders' original mission.
cards.takeaway: If preserving a value or mission through growth matters, encode it into governance early. Changing it later is nearly impossible once power is distributed.
